blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Раньше горячую воду отключали два раза за ___ (лето), а нынче - только один.
exercises.prompt: Previously they shut off hot water twice each summer, and now only once.
exercises.why: The preposition за + acc. denotes the time that it takes to accomplish an action: *Он сделает это за неделю. Я прочитал эту книгу за два дня.* «за + acc.» is also used in combination with «до + gen.» to denote the time of one event taking place before some other event: *Он умер за год до войны.* — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lesson 73.  ·  «The preposition ЗА + Acc. denotes the time that it takes to accomplish an action.» — DLI, Lesson 77.
exercises.context: The preposition за + acc. denotes the time that it takes to accomplish an action: *Он сделает это за неделю.

exercises.q: Я не могу сообразить, что это за аккорд на 1:58 ___ (минута). Может кто-нибудь мне помочь?
exercises.prompt: I can't quite figure out what that chord around 1:58 is. Can somebody help me out?
exercises.why: The preposition НА + Prep. is used to indicate the week during which an event takes place. *Я поеду туда на этой неделе. Я поеду туда на будущей неделе. Я был там на прошлой неделе.* (Compare with: "в прошлом месяце", "в прошлом году".) Note also the expression "на (этих) днях". When referred to the past "на днях" means "a few days ago", "the other day": *Я был там на днях.* When referred to the future, it means "within a few days": *Я буду там на днях.* — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lesson 73.  ·  «The preposition НА + Prep. is used to indicate the week during which an event takes place.» — DLI, Lesson 73.
exercises.context: The preposition НА + Prep. is used to indicate the week during which an event takes place.

exercises.q: Чахоткой в XIX ___ (век) называли туберкулёз лёгких.
exercises.prompt: In the 19th century, tuberculosis was called "consumption."
exercises.why: The preposition В + Prepositional is used: (a) to indicate the year or the month (but never the week) in which an event takes place. *В каком месяце (когда) вы были там? Я был там в этом месяце. Я был там в прошлом месяце. Я был там в январе. В каком году (когда?) вы поедете туда? Я поеду туда в этом году. Я поеду туда в будущем году.* — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lesson 73.  ·  «The preposition В + Prepositional is used: (a) to indicate the year or the month (but never the week) … (b) to indicate the beginning, the middle, the end or any other phase of a period.» — DLI, Lesson 73.
exercises.context: The preposition В + Prepositional is used: (a) to indicate the year or the month (but never the week) in which an event takes place.

exercises.q: Фабрика простояла ___ (целый год).
exercises.prompt: The factory has been lying idle for a year.
exercises.why: Notice that the feminine adjectives have the same ending -ой (-ей) for all cases except for the nominative and accusative. — DLI, Lessons 46 and 47.  ·  «The word "every" in time expressions answering the question "how often" … каждый день, каждое утро, каждую среду (acc.)»; «весь день, всё утро, всю неделю (accus.)». — DLI, Lessons 22, 37.
exercises.context: Notice that the feminine adjectives have the same ending -ой (-ей) for all cases except for the nominative and accusative.

exercises.q: Люди жили точно несколько ___ (столетия) назад.
exercises.why: The genitive case has four main uses: to denote possession ('Michael's car', meaning 'the car of Michael'), to denote number ('five apples'), in negative constructions ('there are no books'), and after several important prepositions ('without me'). — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0). From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lesson 23.  ·  From Владимир Короленко, «История моего современника».
exercises.context: The genitive case has four main uses: to denote possession ('Michael's car', meaning 'the car of Michael'), to denote number ('five apples'), in negative constructions ('there are no books'), and after several important prepositions ('without me').

exercises.q: Свидание сегодня по ___ (вечер), это верно.
exercises.why: The preposition по + dat. pl. is used to indicate that something occurs periodically: 1. on a certain day of the week: *По понедельникам я работаю в штабе. По воскресеньям мы отдыхаем.* 2. during a certain time of a day: *По утрам я читаю газету. По вечерам его никогда нет дома.* Note: never «по дням» except when a modifier is used: по целым дням — days on end; по выходным дням — on off-days. — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lesson 73.  ·  «The preposition по + Dat. Pl. is used to indicate that something occurs periodically.» — DLI, Lesson 74.
exercises.context: The preposition по + dat. pl. is used to indicate that something occurs periodically: 1. on a certain day of the week: *По понедельникам я работаю в штабе.

exercises.q: И когда-нибудь, потом, через ___ (годы), с жизнию, может, и поймешь, что они значили.
exercises.why: **Под** also has three minor, unrelated uses for which it calls the accusative case: to denote something as being 'designated' for something else ('That bar is designated for celebrities'), to denote something fake ('artificial furniture', **под обстановку**), or to denote an approximate time ('around the evening', **под вечер**) — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  From Фёдор Достоевский, «Преступление и наказание».

exercises.q: Уже ___ (столетие) назад заменил Мицкевич «изменника» — «ренегатом».
exercises.why: The only rules that are used in the nominative case are those to turn a word into its plural form (each case has its own rules for converting a word into the singular of that case, and into that case's plural form). The nominative case is used when no other case is being used. — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0). From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lesson 16.  ·  From Юрий Тынянов, «Смерть Вазир-Мухтара».
exercises.context: The only rules that are used in the nominative case are those to turn a word into its plural form (each case has its own rules for converting a word into the singular of that case, and into that case's plural form).
